paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of it. The people ask Jeremiah to pray, and they promise, "Whether it is pleasant or unpleasant, we will obey the voice of the LORD our God…" (Jeremiah 42:6). Then the answer comes, and it is a good one: stay, and God says, "I will build you up and not tear you down," and "do not be afraid of the king of Babylon… for I am with you to save you and deliver you from him" (Jeremiah 42:10-11). A promise to obey only counts if you still mean it when you hear what God says.

Now look at what they were really doing. Egypt looked like the safe spot, the place where they would "not see war or hear the sound of the ram's horn or hunger for bread" (Jeremiah 42:14). But Jeremiah tells them the sword and the famine they feared would follow them there (Jeremiah 42:16). I think they were asking God to bless a plan they had already made. Jeremiah says it plainly: "you have deceived yourselves" (Jeremiah 42:20). Friend, you can run from the thing you fear and find it waiting at the door of the place you ran to.

So here's what I want you to carry out of my bakery. Don't pray for direction when you only want a stamp of approval. Ask God what to do like you mean it, and then do it, even when it sounds scarier than the other road. His "Do not be afraid" always comes with "I am with you," and that is a better place to stand than any palm tree in Egypt. And this story isn't over, so keep your oven warm!
